subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Show that the straight lines x + y = 0, 3x + y − 4 = 0 and x + 3y − 4 = 0 form an isosceles triangle.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), book p.156, chapter 3 THE STRAIGHT LINE, Long Answer question 13. **Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work** — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints a chapter-level marks banner over this section but no per-step allocation on any answer. The split rewards the angle route, which is what the word show is asking for: two marks for each of the two angles, one for reading the three slopes, one for comparing the angles and two for the conclusion with its check. This book prints almost no exam-appearance years, so appearances[] is empty — the chapter has long been examined, we simply have no sourced years for this question. Paper position: Maths-1B Section C prints 3 long answer questions at 8 marks each and the student answers any 2, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The vertices were found and the sides measured as an independent check: A(2, −2), B(−2, 2) and C(1, 1) give AB = 4√2, BC = √10 and CA = √10, so the two sides opposite the equal angles really are equal. Each vertex was substituted into both of the lines that meet there. LINES EXPANDED 2026-09-14 (founder direction, modelled on the Maths-2A, Maths-2B and Maths-1A expansions): every move is written on its own line, with the reason or the arithmetic shown before it is used; the steps, marks and split are unchanged.

steps.why: The angle formula gives the acute angle θ between two lines, and the interior angle at a vertex is either θ or 180° − θ. Two angles of one triangle cannot add to 180° and cannot both be obtuse, so ∠A and ∠B are both θ.
common_mistakes: Writing ∠A = ∠B from tan A = tan B without saying why neither angle is 180° − θ.
Claiming the triangle is equilateral because two angles agree.
steps.memory_tip: Each interior angle is θ or 180° − θ. Two angles of a triangle cannot add to 180°, so equal acute angles here mean ∠A = ∠B.
